The TRACE_FILE variable sets tron::perfetto_trace_dest in pos_startup_host() (src/pos/driver.cpp). The default is "traced".

With TRACE_FILE unset or "traced", the SIGUSR1 tracer joins a traced session, and a set TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES then ends rinzler. With TRACE_FILE naming a path, the capture records in-process and TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES applies (line 301). Line 269 lists this case.

The sampler is off by default. Set TRON_HW_SAMPLER=1 to get any hw counter.

On Intel, temperature updates about once per second whatever TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS is, because coretemp caches each sensor read. Frequency and power follow the interval.
TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS tunes the 100 ms sampler interval.

Section "Selecting categories in-process". In-process captures (runtron --trace FILE, --trace-gen FILE, the SIGUSR1 tracer when TRACE_FILE names a path, and rinzler FUSE captures that set no categories) take their category selection from TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES (lines 267-272).

Example: TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES="+memory,-loading,-driver-detail". The value is a comma-separated list of category names, each with a sign. "+" adds to enabled_categories and "-" to disabled_categories. A trailing "*" is a prefix wildcard and an exact name beats a wildcard (lines 279-290). Unset or empty changes nothing. An entry with no sign, a wildcard not at the end, or an unknown name aborts the run at startup. Setting it for a "traced" session is an error that ends rinzler (lines 292-304).
In-process captures enable the memory category with TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES=+memory.

A FUSE capture start that sets no categories uses TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES, as set when rinzler starts. A bad value fails every such capture until rinzler restarts with a good one. Line 68 points to the README.perfetto.md section.

With TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES unset or empty, the in-process backend keeps the default Perfetto tags, which omit driver-detail and memory. Set it for in-process category selection (line 98). Lines 288 and 388 repeat this.

TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN=N, for phased tracing (--trace-gen) only. A positive integer defers the start of tracing until the total token position, prompt plus generated tokens, crosses N. Unset or 0 starts at prompt-parse completion. If N is at or below the prompt length, tracing starts at parse completion. --trace ignores it and --trace-passes overrides it (lines 143-153). Example on line 154.

trace_from_token() in stream_generate.hpp reads TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN once (static), as max(0, atoi), default 0. Set it before the process starts. --trace and SIGUSR1 ignore it (lines 123-125). Line 112 is the section heading.

If TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN exceeds the token count of the completed run, the result is a small bounded trace, not a deadlock (starts on line 391). Line 40: --trace-passes overrides the variable. Line 364 is an example.
--trace-passes overrides --trace and TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN.
Recipe for a decode steady-state capture: TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN=N nix run .#tronperf -- --gen ... Lines 209, 263, 306 and 314 use the variable to exclude warmup.

Dice payload launch: the launch-child helper "runs root-side code with a fixed environment, then applies uid/gid/groups, cwd, file-mode mask, and the captured submitter env before `exec`" (lines 419-421). Each payload runs as a transient dice-payload-<id>.service started with systemd-run.

Every token that appears in an environment context was read in place. The list holds every tracked *.md file. Result: the documentation names 123 environment variable names (one of them is the wildcard family TRON_BOOK_*). ALREADY DONE? No. No Markdown file is a general environment variable reference. README.dependencies.md:368 refers to an "env var table" in README.ci.md. README.ci.md has no such table at this commit, so that reference is stale. README.md:485, doc/dice.md:100 and doc/distributed-dice-agent-guide.md:116 say it does. The two texts may describe two different readers. (5) Log level: README.tokenizers.md:242 says to set SPDLOG_LEVEL=debug. CHANGELOG.md:405 says the log level is set with TRON_LOG_LEVEL. No document describes TRON_LOG_LEVEL values.
